source_snapshot.procedure: Check the Error Source Record Table (BERT/ERST/HEST) under the OS.
source_snapshot.criteria: It should be found in dmesg log.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: Grep dmesg and /sys/firmware/acpi/tables for BERT, ERST, HEST, or ACPI Error over an SSH command that embeds a password and disables host-key checking.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify that the platform's expected ACPI Platform Error Interface tables—BERT, ERST, and HEST as applicable—are exposed to and recognized by the operating system.
original_test_intent.target: The identified SUT's firmware-provided ACPI tables and the running OS/kernel view of those tables.
original_test_intent.scope: Read-only presence and OS-recognition evidence for BERT, ERST, and HEST; this case does not inject an error or prove that the error-record mechanisms function end to end.
original_test_intent.operation: Record platform identity, list the relevant ACPI table files, capture table headers/content when permitted, and correlate kernel boot messages without clearing logs.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One read-only inspection of the running OS; source timing is 10 attended and 10 machine minutes.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Every table required by the approved platform/architecture RAS specification is present and valid, and the kernel shows no unexpected ACPI/APEI initialization error.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Platform/architecture/BIOS/kernel identity, approved expected-table matrix, relevant sysfs table entries and hashes/headers, complete contextual kernel messages, command status, permissions, and interpretation of absent or optional tables.
ambiguities: The source does not say whether all three tables are mandatory or which are conditional for this platform.
The singular criterion `It should be found in dmesg` does not identify which table or message must appear.
Firmware table presence does not guarantee that the kernel will print each table signature in dmesg.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly keeps the inspection read-only, uses sysfs plus kernel logs, makes acpidump optional, preserves complete output, and requires platform expectations. It still describes the objective as finding table names or messages in logs without clearly separating firmware-table presence, kernel recognition, and functional error-record validation.

applicable_history.decision: Read-only evidence collection remains automatable; missing expected values are readiness inputs and do not erase the ability to collect actual values.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Evidence collection is fully automatable and low risk. A platform owner must define which of BERT, ERST, and HEST are required and what OS-recognition evidence is acceptable; absent tables cannot be judged generically, and this inspection must not be reported as an error-injection or end-to-end RAS test.

available_now: The OS location and named ACPI tables are explicit; sysfs listing, checksums, table headers, and kernel-log collection are read-only.
Actual table presence and kernel messages can be collected before the expectation matrix is supplied, but no PASS may be declared.
missing_inputs: Platform architecture/model, BIOS/firmware build, kernel/OS, and enabled RAS feature configuration
Approved required/conditional/unsupported matrix for BERT, ERST, and HEST
Acceptance rule for table validity and kernel recognition, including whether a dmesg signature is mandatory
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The platform firmware/RAS owner supplies the expected-table matrix and acceptance rule; the OS owner supplies kernel support/configuration context when a table is not exposed or recognized.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: List and hash `/sys/firmware/acpi/tables/{BERT,ERST,HEST}` when present and record permission/absence explicitly
Capture full contextual dmesg/journal APEI/ACPI initialization messages and optionally use an approved acpidump build without modifying firmware state
prohibited_until_closed: Do not clear logs, inject errors, write ACPI/APEI state, infer functional RAS coverage from table presence, or treat an empty grep as success
Do not embed SSH passwords, disable host-key verification, or declare a platform defect before applying the architecture-specific expectation matrix
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner maps each table to required, conditional, or not applicable for the exact platform and defines acceptable table/header/kernel evidence; the agent then compares the captured actual state without extrapolating to error handling.

revision_candidate.test_name: OS Exposure of Expected ACPI BERT, ERST, and HEST Tables
revision_candidate.purpose: Confirm that each ACPI error-record table required for the exact platform is exposed by firmware and recognized by the running OS without unexpected APEI initialization errors.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The identified server architecture, BIOS/firmware build, OS/kernel, and enabled RAS configuration. Table requirements are architecture- and platform-specific.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Firmware-provided BERT, ERST, and HEST tables and their OS/kernel exposure only; no hardware error injection or persistence/recovery function is exercised.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Platform identity and architecture, BIOS/firmware and kernel versions, RAS configuration, required/conditional/not-applicable table matrix, and acceptance rule for table validity and kernel recognition.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Using authorized read-only access, list the exact BERT/ERST/HEST entries in `/sys/firmware/acpi/tables`, capture safe metadata or approved raw dumps, and collect full contextual ACPI/APEI kernel messages. Record command status and distinguish absent, inaccessible, invalid, and not-applicable results.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Verified SUT/OS identity, readable kernel logs and ACPI table path, protected remote access, preserved log history, and the platform expectation matrix for final judgment.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Identity/version baseline, expected-table matrix, table names/sizes/hashes/headers or approved dumps, contextual dmesg/journal output, permission and command status, unexpected ACPI errors, and per-table comparison result.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform's firmware/RAS specification. ACPI defines BERT, HEST, and ERST mechanisms but does not require the same table set on every server configuration.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Read-only inspection only; do not clear logs, write firmware/ACPI state, inject errors, use unverified SSH endpoints, expose credentials, or claim end-to-end RAS validation.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: No approval is needed for authorized read-only collection; the platform owner must provide the expectation matrix and adjudicate unexplained absence or initialization errors.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Collection, parsing, and matrix comparison are automatable. Platform applicability and final interpretation of unexpected firmware/kernel behavior remain engineering decisions.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No device-state recovery is expected. On access/identity/permission anomalies, stop, preserve the outputs, and request corrected access or platform mapping.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: SUT identity mismatch, unprotected credentials, unavailable read-only evidence, command/permission failure that obscures presence, missing expectation matrix for final judgment, or evidence of an unexpected ACPI/APEI initialization error requiring owner review.

identified_defects: The source conflates named ACPI table existence with appearance of a table name in dmesg.
The source gives no platform-specific required/conditional table matrix.
DeepSeek's SSH example exposes a password and disables host-key verification.
Neither source nor V2 explicitly excludes false claims of end-to-end RAS functionality from a static table-presence check.
reason_for_change: Make table presence, kernel recognition, and functional RAS validation distinct, while retaining safe collection even before the platform expectation is known.

new_technical_evidence.title: ACPI Specification 6.6, Platform Error Interfaces
new_technical_evidence.supports: HEST describes hardware error sources to the OS, BERT reports boot error records, and ERST defines serialized error-record operations; these tables have different purposes.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The specification does not establish the exact product's required table set or dmesg strings.

new_technical_evidence.title: Linux Kernel Documentation: ACPI Tables on arm64
new_technical_evidence.supports: BERT/HEST are tied to RAS support and ERST applicability can be conditional; requirements differ by architecture and boot environment.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The source testcase does not identify the SUT architecture, so arm64 rules must not be applied to x86 platforms.

removed_ambiguities: Separates presence, kernel recognition, and end-to-end function.
Requires a per-platform table matrix instead of assuming all servers expose all three.
Defines collection before expected values as evidence-only, not PASS.
resolved_blockers: Missing acpica-tools is not a blocker when sysfs and kernel-log evidence are sufficient; the package is optional for a deeper dump.
remaining_blockers: Final acceptance remains pending the exact platform expectation matrix and resolution of any missing/inaccessible/invalid table evidence.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves V2's safe automated collection but corrects the semantic boundary: a sysfs table, a kernel message, and proven RAS behavior are different claims. It also makes architecture-specific applicability and no-false-completion explicit.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source names BERT, ERST, and HEST and says they should be found in dmesg under the OS.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 adds sysfs evidence; V3 explicitly prevents table presence from being misreported as end-to-end RAS validation and requires platform applicability.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Collect sysfs/table/kernel evidence without clearing logs, injecting errors, weakening SSH verification, or claiming PASS before applying the platform matrix.
